To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the concentration of copper appearing in xylem ex-udate is buffered against external changes in concentration, (2) copper is not transported as a free cupric ion, (3) manganese is transported as a free divalent metal ion, and (4) copper and manganese absorption does not require a special mechanism other than that necessary for maintaining the transmembrane electrical potential.

1) the concentrations of copper and manganese in the xylex sap are not linearly related to their concentrations in the external solution; 2) copper is not absorbed by a metabolically-linked mechanism; and 3) the concentrations of manganese and copper in the xylemic sap are not linear related to their concentrations on the root surface.
Copper and manganese in the xylemic stream are transported to the xylemic exudate by passive diffusion, and that no special metabolitically-linked mechanism need to be postulated to explain this.
